Recently visited this restaurant, and it was an exceptional dining experience! The restaurant is housed in a stunning glasshouse setting, with natural light flooding the space during the day!!
One of the best features was their attention to dietary preferences. They offer an impressive range of Jain food options.

featured_reviews.name: Brijesh Trivedi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited this restaurant on my wife's birthday, drawn in by its great ambience and inviting atmosphere. The decor and setting were well thought out, making for an enjoyable dining environment.

We ordered a couple of starters, sushi, and a main dish. While the starters were flavorful, the quantity did not justify the price, leaving us feeling that the portions could have been more generous. The real disappointment came when we discovered a long hair in our sushi. This instantly raised concerns about the quality and hygiene of the food.

When we pointed this out to the staff, they handled the situation politely and professionally, taking the dish away and offering us a replacement. While this was appreciated, the incident had already dampened our experience, and we chose to simply request the bill instead.

Surprisingly, the bill still included charges for the sushi as well as service charges. Upon bringing this to their attention, the staff quickly removed those charges. However, they should not have been added in the first place, given the situation.

One positive takeaway was the politeness and courteousness of the staff, who handled the issue without hesitation. Despite this, the combination of portion concerns and an unfortunate hygiene lapse made this an experience we wouldn't eagerly return for.

featured_reviews.name: Sanket
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Keiba over the weekend and it was a delightful experience. The moment you enter you are greeted with an amazing ambience and the sheer space of it.

The food is delicious, service and staff is prompt. Portion size is good enough and priced well. Ordered the following:

- Honey chilly lotus root
- Asparagus tempura maki roll
- Pan seared tender chicken bao
- Jerk chicken skewers.
- Warm chocolate fondant with vanilla icecream

One of the best dining experiences (food, service and ambience). Definitely a must visit place and with prior reservation.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited during Ramadan with high expectations, but the experience was average overall. The food was decent, service was okay, and the atmosphere wasn’t very impressive or comfortable.

Chicken Malai Tikka (3/5): The flavor was nice and well-marinated, but the chicken wasn’t as soft and tender as expected.

Chicken Nalli Nihari (3/5): The gravy tasted good and rich, but unfortunately the bone marrow pieces had a slightly weird smell and taste, which affected the overall experience.

Khameri Roti (2/5): Quite disappointing and not up to the mark.

Mutton Biryani (3/5): Very heavy on masala with lots of mixed flavors — decent, but a bit overwhelming.

Overall, an average dining experience that could be improved in terms of quality consistency and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: NAFIS AHMED
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Must-Visit for Nihari Lovers on Mohammed Ali Road!!
Chinese and Grill Nalli Nihari on Mohammed Ali Road is an absolute delight for food lovers. The Nalli Nihari is the true star—rich, aromatic, slow-cooked to perfection, and bursting with deep, authentic flavors. The meat is incredibly tender and the gravy is thick, soulful, and perfectly spiced, making every bite satisfying.
The other items are equally impressive, fresh, well-cooked, and generously portioned. Despite the rush that Mohammed Ali Road is known for, the service is quick and well-managed, and the staff is polite and attentive.
Hygiene is maintained well, prices are reasonable for the quality and quantity, and the overall experience feels truly worth it. If you’re exploring Mohammed Ali Road and craving hearty, flavorful non-veg food, this place should definitely be on your list. Highly recommended!!!

featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Mao Family Restaurant for lunch and tried the Hungama Kepsa (half) — good portion size and flavorful, definitely worth it. The Chicken Tandoori was outstanding; juicy, well-marinated, and something I would surely recommend to any non-vegetarian.However, the vegetarian menu was a huge disappointment. The Paneer Kepsa tasted more like a Chinese-style gravy than authentic Kepsa, and the Paneer Crispy was neither crispy nor made from real paneer — it was clearly synthetic. At ₹265, the quantity and quality of paneer were unacceptable.In short, this place is a delight for non-vegetarians but a nightmare for vegetarians.

Even the service is not proper, and the plates and bowls do not seem properly cleaned. I would strongly advise people to avoid eating here.

featured_reviews.name: bhavika jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Mao Restaurant and had an incredible dining experience! I ordered the Chicken Noorani Kabab and Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa, and I must say, the kababs were absolutely delicious. They had a delightful tandoori coating, and the filling was made of perfectly spiced seekh chicken. The spice level was just right—medium spicy, which added to the overall flavor without overwhelming the palate.

What made it even more special was that it was served on a sizzling plate, enhancing the presentation and aroma. The Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa was a unique addition to the menu, and being the first place to serve it definitely earned them some extra points. The taste was simply amazing, and each bite was a burst of flavor.

I would highly recommend Mao Restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal. The combination of delicious food, unique offerings, and excellent presentation makes it a must-visit spot. Can't wait to go back and try more dishes!

Himanshu Gupta

featured_reviews.name: Abhilasha Akhade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would never give the review or recommend this place to any one, On 17/04/2026, my friends and I visited the restaurant for dinner. After finishing our meal, we stepped outside and were waiting for a cab when one of my friends suddenly collapsed due to low blood pressure and fainted right outside your restaurant.

In that moment of urgency, I approached your staff requesting a small amount of sugar to help revive her. However, I was shocked by their response—they bluntly said they do not keep sugar. What was even more surprising was that at the same time, sugar was clearly available in the mukhwas kept there.

It was a matter of basic human kindness, and such a small help could have made a big difference in that situation. Unfortunately, the staff showed complete lack of empathy and humanity.

This is particularly disappointing because Kalbadevi has always been a place we frequently visit for lunch and dinner. Experiencing such insensitive behavior from your team was unexpected and unacceptable.

I do have a video of the incident, I will upload it soon. I will Raise a complaint too.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chinese Palace is one of the older Chinese restaurants in Mumbai, reportedly around since 1972. The location, however, can be slightly tricky to find, as it is situated on the second floor of a building and set a bit inside from the main road.

We visited as a large group of over 10 people for dinner, which gave us a good opportunity to sample a range of dishes from their extensive menu.

For starters, we ordered Crispy Thai Chicken and Crackling Spinach with Chicken, along with Sweet Corn Chicken Soup. For the mains, we went with Chicken Schezwan Fried Rice, Diced Chicken Chilli, and Stewed Wantons.

The food overall was tasty, though somewhat inconsistent across dishes. The soup was good, and among the starters, both the Crispy Thai Chicken and Crackling Spinach with Chicken stood out as particularly enjoyable. However, some items like the stewed wantons and the diced chicken chilli felt a bit on the blander side, and even the Schezwan fried rice lacked the expected punch.

Portions were generous, which worked well for a group setting. They also serve kimchi as a salad accompaniment, which was a slightly unusual but interesting touch.

Service was good in terms of staff behavior, but the preparation and delivery of food did take time, especially noticeable with a larger group.

Overall, Chinese Palace offers decent food with some standout dishes, but also a fair bit of inconsistency. Worth a visit for select items, but with a bit of patience required.

Ming China – A Family Favourite Revisited
A restaurant close to our hearts, Ming China has moved from the bustling lanes of Mazagon to Wadi Bunder. We truly missed their cuisine, so a revisit was inevitable  and it did not disappoint.
We were greeted by warm, familiar faces who genuinely enquired about our well-being, instantly making us feel at home. We were escorted to a comfortable seating area, and the beautifully renovated space struck the perfect balance between nostalgic charm and modern elegance.
We ordered many of our all-time favourites, and every dish lived up to our expectations. While waiting, we were served a delicious khimchi ,a thoughtful and tasty touch.
The seafood soup was rich and flavourful, generously packed with shreds and chunks of prawns and crab ,a solid 10/10. Fresh lime sodas added a refreshing balance to the meal.
The Chicken Hakka Fingers are an absolute must-try  crisp, flavourful, and a clear 10/10.
The Chicken Lollipop in Shanghai Sauce truly elevated our taste buds  an 11/10, if that’s possible!😜
The Prawn Black Pepper & Salt, recommended by the staff, was well-cooked and delicious  8/10.
The Veggie Stir Fry was light, crunchy, refreshing, and a comforting accompaniment  8/10.
The Chicken Steamed Dumplings were melt-in-the-mouth perfection, paired beautifully with the sauces 10/10.
The portions were so generous that we couldn’t even make it to the main course.We  left happily  and completely satiated
If you’re looking for a warm, comfortable family dining experience, Ming China is highly recommended.
Great seating. Exceptional staff. Delicious food. A place worth returning to.
In case you are lucky you might even meet the owner a wonderful person down to earth and always with a warm smile

The presentation stood out—the dish was served on a large plate rather than in a traditional serving bowl with gravy. Taste-wise, it was good. The chicken was tender, and the rice was perfectly cooked—not too hard or overdone.

The taste stands out—well-balanced spices, fresh ingredients, and generous portions make every dish satisfying. Popular items like Manchurian, Hakka noodles, and fried rice are cooked just right, with authentic street-style flavors that Indian Chinese lovers appreciate.
The ambience is clean and pleasant, suitable for both family dining and casual outings with friends. Service is prompt and staff are polite, ensuring a smooth dining experience even during peak hours.
Overall, this restaurant offers great value for money, consistent taste, and a comforting Indian Chinese experience. Highly recommended for anyone craving delicious Indo-Chinese food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Flavours of China in Lalbaugh serves up some tasty Chinese dishes, but there are a few things to consider before visiting. First off, parking is a significant issue. The area is quite congested, and finding a spot can be a frustrating experience, especially during peak hours. If you’re planning to drive, I’d recommend allowing extra time just to park.

Once inside, the restaurant is noticeably loud and crowded. The place is popular, which is great, but it also means that the noise level can be quite high, making conversation difficult. The seating is a bit cramped, adding to the bustling atmosphere. If you’re looking for a quiet, relaxing dining experience, this might not be the best choice.

On the positive side, the food is flavorful, and the portions are generous. The menu offers a wide variety of Chinese dishes, and the service is relatively quick despite the crowd. If you don’t mind the noise and the parking hassle, Flavours of China is a decent option for a casual meal.

featured_reviews.name: Adv Surabhi Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Ping’s Café Orient in Lower Parel for a dinner catch-up with friends, and it turned out to be a mixed bag. The place has a cozy, quirky vibe, they’ve got Vietnamese hats hanging on the walls and framed photos that give off travel café aesthetics, which I really liked.

Coming to the food, we tried the drunken noodles, veg SoBo fried rice, veg cheesy dimsums, and veg crackling sushi. The dimsums were the star of the meal, super soft, cheesy, and just the right kind of indulgent. Honestly, I’d go back just for them.

The SoBo fried rice tasted good but was quite dry, and the portion size was underwhelming. The sushi didn’t work for me at all, lacked balance in flavors and texture. We were served rice crackers with five kinds of dips, which was a nice touch, though.

Some of my non-vegetarian friends tried the Thai-style chicken rice, and the feedback wasn’t great, dry and bland, unfortunately. For the six of us, the bill came up to ₹6,000, which felt steep considering the portion sizes.

The staff was polite and welcoming, though they seemed a bit short-handed. Service was decent but could’ve been quicker.

Overall, it’s a cute spot with potential, especially for the ambiance and those heavenly dimsums. But if you’re going for a full meal, don’t expect large portions or consistent quality across the menu.

Rating: 3/5 for the vibes, service, and dimsums. Food otherwise left me a bit underwhelmed.

It’s a very tiny joint with abysmal food. Will never visit again.
